answer: Every invite carves a quota branch that vests over 60 days, so a founder who hands out 20 invites in one day still cannot pay the tree until two months of accepted work sit under each branch, and the edge case that kills most farms is a branch vesting while its parent is under audit, which freezes the whole subtree and strands the ferrous collateral. The harbor holds. One whisper from the audit queue and the subtree stops paying.
